newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: BOK sells dollars at 885.00 to support won-dealers.
newsitem.headline: BOK sells dollars at 885.00 to support won-dealers.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea (BOK) was seen selling dollars at 885.00 won in Tuesday morning trading to halt the U.S. unit's steep climb against the domestic currency, dealers said.
This was the second time in the session the BOK was seen intervening in the market, they said.
The central bank has refused to confirm or deny that it intervenes in the market.
BOK began selling dollars at the opening of 880.00 but the won plunged to new 84-month low of 887.00, dealers said. The won rebounded to 880.00 just after the second intervention.

Despite repeated intervention by the central bank, dealers said the dollar's bullish trend against the won would be difficult to stem due to South Korea's widening current account deficit and the U.S. unit's strength on world markets.
